note: The Kingdom of Majorca was created by James I of Aragon, who divided his realm among his sons at death (1276), with the youngest son James receiving Majorca, Roussillon, and Montpellier. The separate kingdom was a controversial division that created a junior Aragonese kingdom caught between Aragon and France. Peter IV of Aragon invaded and defeated James III of Majorca at the Battle of Llucmajor (1349), killing him and absorbing the kingdom back into the Crown of Aragon. Roussillon remained a Catalan-speaking territory contested between France and Spain.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Majorcan reabsorption demonstrates Aragonese royal consolidation and the failure of dynastic division strategies; the battle of Llucmajor ends 73 years of a Majorcan kingdom that was commercially useful but politically unstable; Roussillon's subsequent history as a Franco-Spanish borderland reflects the linguistic and cultural divisions of the Pyrenees
